what_its_for: Chlorpromazine is used to treat mental health conditions such as schizophrenia and other psychotic disorders (conditions where you may hear, see, or believe things that are not real). It is also used to control severe nausea and vomiting, hiccups that won't stop, and to help manage certain behavior problems. Your doctor may also use it before surgery to help you relax.
how_to_take: Take chlorpromazine exactly as your doctor tells you. You can take it with food or a glass of milk to help prevent stomach upset. Swallow tablets whole with a full glass of water. Do not crush or chew the tablets unless your doctor says it is okay. If you are taking a liquid form, measure your dose carefully using the measuring device that comes with your medicine — do not use a regular kitchen spoon. Try to take it at the same time(s) every day to keep a steady level in your body.
dosing: Your dose will be decided by your doctor based on your condition, age, weight, and how you respond to the medicine. Doses vary widely — adults may start at 10 mg to 25 mg taken 2 to 4 times a day, and your doctor may slowly increase the dose if needed. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions. Never change your dose or stop taking this medicine without talking to your doctor first, even if you feel better.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember — unless it is almost time for your next scheduled dose. In that case, skip the missed dose and take your next dose at the regular time. Do not take two doses at once to make up for a missed one. If you are unsure what to do, call your pharmacist or doctor.
storage: Store chlorpromazine tablets at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C and 25°C). Keep it away from heat, direct light, and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep the liquid form away from freezing temperatures. Keep all medicine out of reach of children and pets. Do not use medicine that has changed color, appears cloudy (for liquids), or has expired. Ask your pharmacist how to safely dispose of unused medicine.
what_to_avoid: Avoid drinking alcohol while taking chlorpromazine — it can dangerously increase drowsiness and dizziness. Do not drive, operate heavy machinery, or do anything that requires you to be alert until you know how this medicine affects you, as it can cause strong drowsiness. Avoid getting too hot — chlorpromazine can make it harder for your body to regulate temperature, so be careful in hot weather, during exercise, or in hot baths or saunas. Avoid prolonged sun exposure and use sunscreen and protective clothing when outdoors, as this medicine can make your skin more sensitive to sunlight. Avoid standing up too quickly, especially when getting out of bed, to prevent dizziness or fainting. Tell your doctor or pharmacist about all other medicines, vitamins, and herbal supplements you take, as many can interact with chlorpromazine.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you experience: uncontrollable movements of your face, tongue, or body (such as lip smacking, grimacing, or repetitive movements); muscle stiffness, high fever, sweating, fast heartbeat, or confusion (signs of a rare but serious condition called Neuroleptic Malignant Syndrome); fainting or severe dizziness; difficulty swallowing or breathing; skin or eyes turning yellow (jaundice); signs of infection such as fever, chills, or sore throat; seizures; or thoughts of harming yourself. Also call your doctor if you notice worsening symptoms, new side effects, or any concerns about your treatment.
when_it_works: Chlorpromazine does not work immediately for all conditions. For nausea and vomiting or hiccups, it may work within 30 to 60 minutes. For mental health conditions like schizophrenia, it may take several days to a few weeks before you notice the full benefit. It is important to keep taking your medicine as directed even if you do not feel better right away. Do not stop taking it without talking to your doctor, as stopping suddenly can make your condition worse.
special_populations: Older adults: Older patients are more sensitive to side effects such as dizziness, falls, drowsiness, and certain movement problems. Doctors usually start with a lower dose. Older adults with dementia-related behavior problems should generally NOT use this medicine as it may increase the risk of stroke or death — discuss risks carefully with your doctor. Children: Chlorpromazine can be used in children but the dose is carefully calculated based on weight. It should not be used in children under 6 months old. Pregnancy: This medicine may harm the unborn baby and newborns may experience withdrawal symptoms or movement problems if the mother took it late in pregnancy. Talk to your doctor immediately if you are pregnant or plan to become pregnant. Breastfeeding: Chlorpromazine passes into breast milk and may harm a nursing baby. Talk to your doctor before breastfeeding. Liver or kidney problems: Your doctor may need to adjust your dose if you have liver or kidney disease.
